correctness.rationale: The two-step kernel is a stochastic matrix product of binomial weights and exact binomial cell integrals. Both factors are TP2; Cauchy–Binet makes their product TP2, so pairwise transition TV reduces to an ordered upper-tail difference, maximized by the endpoint pair. Reflection supplies exact endpoint overlap and an attaining high-index cell indicator. A uniform upper-tail ratio at most 1/n and the beta-concentration substitution give both parity-specific asymptotic constants e^{-1/2}. Exact rational transition tests for 1<=n<=14 validate many finite consequences; the proof, not finite testing, covers all n.

value.rationale: The oscillation quotient is a natural Markov-kernel mixing/stability invariant. An exact first strict contraction time is mathematically motivated because \(K_n\) alone has disjoint endpoint supports and coefficient one. The theorem supplies sharp attained finite-n constants and a highly non-obvious super-exponentially small second-step overlap, contrasting the familiar degree-dependent spectral derivative behavior. The precise finite overlap is reusable as a benchmark for high-degree iteration; no external application or larger theorem is claimed.
